summary: When Mordecai perceives all that was done (Haman's decree to destroy Jews), rends clothes puts on sackcloth ashes goes into city wailing, comes to king's gate sackcloth not allowed in, in every province Jews fast weep wail sackcloth ashes spread under many. Esther's maids and eunuchs tell her, queen exceedingly grieved, sends raiment to clothe Mordecai sackcloth off but he refused, calls Hathach eunuch appointed to attend and commands go to Mordecai know what and why, Mordecai tells about sum of money Haman promised and shows copy of writing of decree to destroy Jews to show Esther and declares to her and charges her to go to king make supplication and plead for people. Esther says all know whoever whether man or woman who goes to inner court to king who not called there is one law to be put to death except king hold out golden scepter that he may live, and I have not been called to come to king these 30 days. They tell Mordecai Esther's words, Mordecai says think not you will escape in king's house more than all Jews, for if you keep silence now then relief and deliverance will arise to Jews from another place but you and father's house will perish, and who knows whether you have come to kingdom for such a time as this? Esther says go gather all Jews in Shushan fast for me three days night and day I also and my maidens will fast likewise and so will I go to king which is not according to law and if I perish I perish. Mordecai went his way did according to all Esther commanded.
whyItMatters: Most famous line 'for such a time as this' — Esther's dilemma, Mordecai's charge, fasting before risky approach to king, if I perish I perish.

questions.question: Why does Mordecai wear sackcloth and why can't he enter king's gate?
questions.answer: Sackcloth and ashes is mourning and protest attire, public lament after Haman's decree to annihilate Jews with date set and money paid. Comes to king's gate but sackcloth not allowed to come into king's gate — law that mourning attire not allowed in palace precinct to maintain image of invulnerability. So Mordecai wails loudly in city at gate threshold, visible but not entering. In every province Jews have same fast weep wail sackcloth ashes spread under many — communal mourning.

questions.question: What is copy of decree and money Haman promised?
questions.answer: Haman cast Pur (lot) to set date Adar 13 to destroy, kill, annihilate all Jews young old children women, spoil goods, and promised to pay 10,000 talents silver into king's treasuries for loss. Copy of writing of decree given in Shushan to be destroyed — public edict. Mordecai shows Esther copy to show her and charges her to go to king make supplication and plead. Esther's first response is legal fear: any man or woman who goes to inner court not called one law to die unless king holds out golden scepter, and I have not been called 30 days — risk, and king may not be favorably disposed, plus approaching uncalled is capital crime.

questions.question: What does Mordecai mean 'If you keep silence deliverance will arise from another place but you and father's house will perish, who knows for such a time as this?'
questions.answer: Mordecai says think not you will escape in king's house more than all Jews (being queen won't protect if Jews destroyed). If keep silence (remain safe), relief and deliverance (revach and hatzala) will arise to Jews from another place — confidence that God will provide deliverance somehow, even if not through Esther, but you and father's house will perish — lose opportunity. Who knows whether for such a time as this you have come to kingdom? — suggests providence, not coincidence, that Esther became queen at this time for this purpose. Does not mention God explicitly (Esther never mentions God), but implies providential placement. Esther's response: gather all Jews in Shushan fast for me three days night and day I and maidens likewise then I will go which is not according to law and if I perish I perish — resolve after communal fasting. Fasting before risky obedience as seeking favor.
